senses.gloss: दक्षिण- + अग्नि दक्षिण- + अग्नि, m. one kind of sacred fire, that which is taken from the domestic fire and is placed to the south.
दक्षिणा- + अग्र दक्षिणा- + अग्र, adj. that of which the points are directed southward.
दक्षिणा- + अभिमुख दक्षिणा- + अभिमुख, adj. turned to the south, Man. 4, 50.
दक्षिणा-अभि- + मुख दक्षिणा-अभि- + मुख, adj. the same, Man. 4, 50.

दक्षिणा- + अयन दक्षिणा- + अयन,
 I. n. the half of the year when the sun moves to the south of the equator, Man. 1, 67.
 II. adj. lying on the course of the sun to the south of the equator, Bhāg. P. 5, 23, 5.
दक्षिण- + आचार दक्षिण- + आचार, adj. conducting one's self honestly, MBh. 4, 167.
दक्षिणा- + आवर्त दक्षिणा- + आवर्त, adj. 1. turned to the et Bhāg. P. 5, 23, 5. 2. turned the south, MBh. 6, 5671.
दक्षिण- + उत्तर दक्षिण- + उत्तर, turned to the south and to the north, Mārk. P. 16, 34.
दक्षिण- + कूल दक्षिण- + कूल, adj., f. ला, the bank of which is turned toward the south, Bhāg. P. 1, 19, 17.
दकोदर दकोदर, i. e. दक (for उदक), -उदर, n. A dropsical belly, Suśr. 1, 92, 16.

दक्ष् दक्ष्, i. 1, Par. ved. To act in a satisfying manner.
 --Ātm.
 1. To be strong, Lass. 101, 15 (read दक्षते) = Rigv. vii. 16, 6, ved.
 2. † To increase.
 3. To act quickly.
 4. To go or move.
 5. † To hurt.

दक्ष दक्ष् + अ,
 I. adj., f. षा.
 1. Clever, able, Man. 7, 61; 5, 150.
 2. [] Suitable, Bhāg. P. 4, 6, 44.
 II. m. One of the Prajāpatis, sons of Brahman, Man. 9, 128; MBh. 1, 2574.
 --Cf. दक्षिण; δεξιός, δεξιτερός; Lat. dexter; Goth. taihsvs. O.H.G. zeso.

दाक्ष दाक्ष, i. e. दक्ष + अ,
 I. adj. Referring to Dakṣa, Hariv. 7444.
 II. m. or n. South, Man. 6, 10 (with अयन, The sacrifice ordained for the winter solstice).
दक्षता दक्ष + ता, f. Cleverness, Sāh. D. 90.

दक्षिण दक्षिण, i. e. दक्ष् + इन,
 I. adj., f. णा.
 1. Clever, Śatr. 14, 56.
 2. Right (not left), Rām. 2, 52, 86; with परि-इ, To walk round a person or thing, keeping the right hand towards them, Bhāg. P. 4, 12, 25; with कृ, To show one's reverence in this manner, 1, 14, 13.
 3. South, southern, Man. 3, 258.
 4. Upright, honest, MBh. 4, 167.
 II. m. and n.
 1. The right side, Rām. 2, 92, 13.
 2. South, Nal. 9, 23.
 III. f. णा.
 1. A good milch cow (ved.).
 2. Legitimate possession(?), Man. 8, 349.
 3. A present to Brāhmaṇas, as a sacrificial fee, Man. 8, 207.
 4. Fee, MBh. 5, 3779.
 5. Gift, Man. 3, 141.
 IV. दक्षिणेन, instr. adv.
 1. Southward, Bhāg. P. 5, 17, 9.
 2. To the right hand, 5, 21, 8.
 --Comp.

दक्षिणा दक्षिणा (old instr. sing. of दक्षिण), adv. To the right hand, southward.
 --Cf. दक्षिण.

दक्षिणतस् दक्षिण + तस्, adv.
 1. To the right hand, MBh. 3, 14549.
 2. Southward, Man. 3, 91.
दक्षिणावन्त् दक्षिणा + वन्त्, adj., f. वती, Abounding in presents, MBh. 1, 128.
दक्षिणीय दक्षिणीय, i. e. दक्षिणा + ईय, adj. Worthy to be honored with presents, Hariv. 2780.

दाक्षायण दाक्षायण, i. e. दक्ष + आयन,
 I. patronym., f. णी, A descendant of Dakṣa, Bhāg. P. 6, 5, 2; Śāk. 101, 7.
 II. n.
 1. The posterity of Dakṣa, Bhāg. P. 4, c. 1.
 2. Gold, or a gold ornament; see the next.
दाक्षायणिन् दाक्षायणिन्, i. e. दाक्षायण + इन्, adj., f. नी, Wearing gold ornaments, Yājñ. 1, 133.
दाक्षायण्य दाक्षायण्य, i. e. दाक्षायणी + य, m. The son of Dākṣāyaṇī, MBh. 13, 6831.

दाक्षिणात्य दाक्षिणात्य, i. e. दक्षिणा + त्य + अ,
 I. adj. Southern, MBh. 1, 4690; Pañc. 3, 9.
 II. m.
 1. pl. The nations of the south, Rām. 2, 82, 7.
 2. The south, Hariv. 6200.

दाक्षिण्य दाक्षिण्य, i. e. दक्षिण + य, n.
 1. Politeness, Daśak. in Chr. 180, 17.
 2. Kindness, Bhartṛ. 2, 19.
दाक्ष्य दाक्ष्य, i. e. दक्ष + य, n. Ability, skill, Man. 10, 124.
दक्षिण- + पश्चिम दक्षिण- + पश्चिम, adj. south-western.
दक्षिणतस्-पुरस् दक्षिणतस्-पुरस्, adv. south-eastward, MBh. 2, 1120.
दक्षिण- + पूर्व दक्षिण- + पूर्व, adj., f. वा, south-eastern.
दक्षिणा- + प्रवण दक्षिणा- + प्रवण, adj. with a declivity towards the south, Man. 3, 206.
दक्षिणा- + मुख दक्षिणा- + मुख, adj., f. खी, turned to the south, Man. 2, 52.
दक्ष- + सावर्णि दक्ष- + सावर्णि, m. the ninth Manu, ib. 18.
